liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Help on the Way** (6 reviews): Reviewer sees the return of Help>Slip>Franklin's as the main point of interest, and a pretty good version; First played since 10-11-1977, after six years; played well, and Jerry gets the lyrics right [13][15][16][17][18][19]
- **Let It Grow** (3 reviews): Reviewer thought Let It Grow had a nice feel; Rain actually fell during Let It Grow, and the band seemed to rush for cover at set's end [16][18][20]
- **My Brother Esau** (1 review): Annotated Grateful Dead reportedly says this show was the first time they played it [22]
- **Slipknot!** (1 review): Shorter, concise and energetic version, with Jerry leading the unison riff at the end [15]
- **Franklin's Tower** (1 review): Emerges confidently out of the Slipknot! ending [15]
- **Playing in the Band** (1 review): Playin' is called pretty good [13]

## Setlist highlights

- **Help on the Way**: back after 434 archived shows (1991 days) [25]
- **Slipknot!**: back after 434 archived shows (1991 days) [25]
- Earliest performances in the archive: My Brother Esau [25]

## The recordings

- **gd83-03-25.sbd.miller.23572.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 132 min; rated 2.5/5 by 6 [1]. Said about its sound: Soundboard is of nice quality [17]
- **gd1983-03-25.167107.nak700.kelley.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 134 min [4]
- **gd1983-03-25.157656.senn421.blend.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 132 min [6]
- **gd83-03-25.fob-senn.willy.7350.sbeok.shnf**: source not stated; 21 songs; 132 min; rated 3.19/5 by 16 [9]. Said about its sound: Audience recording is exceptionally good, far better than the sloppy playing it captures; Reviewer calls the sound very, very good; Reviewer, who stood throughout, calls this a stunning audience recording [13][16][19][20]
- **gd1983-03-25.148801.sbd.clugston.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 130 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [10]

## Around the show

- Attendee recalls unusually cool Phoenix weather threatening rain, fitting the Cold Rain and Snow opener [18]
- Reviewer stood near the soundboard before the second set, declining friend Tori's wish to move further back [23]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd83-03-25.sbd.miller.23572.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Reel -> Cass -> Dat -> CD -> EAC -> Samplitude v7.02 Professional -> Cool Edit Pro v2.0 -> SHN [1]. Also: Patched with three Sennheiser 421 audience sources; patched and edited by Charlie Miller [1]
- **gd1983-03-25.167107.nak700.kelley.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Ken Kelley; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Ken Kelley's Master Audience Cassettes; Nakamichi 700 mics > JVC KD-2 w/Super ANRS (Maxell XLII-S90) [4]. Also: Dave Cramer's Sennheiser 421 source patches 1:27 of Drums and 0:08 of Space [4]
- **gd1983-03-25.157656.senn421.blend.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassettes; 3 x Sennheiser 421 mics > unknown mixer > Sony D5M (Maxell XLII-S) [6]. Also: Sennheiser 421 source from Matt Field and Dave Cramer patches 0:29 of the Drums > Space transition [6]
- **gd83-03-25.fob-senn.willy.7350.sbeok.shnf**: source: FOB>3 Senn. 421's>MC>DAT>CD [9]
- **gd1983-03-25.148801.sbd.clugston.flac16**: transferred by Scott Clugston; source: Master Soundboard Cassette > Cassette > PCM [10]. Also: Matt Field's Sennheiser 421 FOB source, the first PCM Dead recording, supplies crowd noise and song openings [10]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by The Music Never Stopped: [Compton Terrace Amphitheater – The Music Never Stopped](https://dayofthedeadshow.home.blog/tag/compton-terrace-amphitheater/) [26]
